report.title: When temporal blocking helps iterative GPU stencils, and when halo and resource costs erase the gain

budget_assessment.judgment: Within the 1,300–1,700-word and seven-primary-URL budgets; the report compares alternatives and includes measured wins, counterexamples, applicability limits, and one explicit analytical caution.

scope_and_novelty_assessment.judgment: Finite and substantively answered, but materially overlaps R835 and its R838 review metadata.
scope_and_novelty_assessment.overlap: R838 records R835 as a 1,784-word knowledge report centered on successive-time reuse, halo/capacity crossover, and measured win/loss cases. Its source verification already covers the same AN5D v4 and EBISU v1 papers, including their V100/A100 depth and 151-versus-197 GCells/s examples. R876 reuses those primary sources and much of the same crossover evidence, while narrowing the synthesis to iterative stencil time depth and adding a compact useful-work model plus an arithmetic audit of EBISU's printed fraction.
scope_and_novelty_assessment.novel_increment: The new report makes its compared design choices explicit in one ledger, states a multiplicative halo useful-work estimate and idealized traffic bound, and independently flags a numerical inconsistency in EBISU's stated 3D valid fraction. These additions are useful archive refinements but do not make the broad scope novel against R835.
scope_and_novelty_assessment.conclusion: Keep as a held knowledge archive. Avoid another generic temporal-blocking or halo-crossover assignment unless a concrete engine question or materially new source set defines it.

depth_and_applicability.judgment: Substantive and coherent; adequate depth for the requested comparison.
depth_and_applicability.strengths: Distinguishes streaming, spatial blocking, N.5D/register or shared-memory blocking, and device-level tiling; separates measured rates from idealized models; explains that overlap, local-memory traffic, synchronization, register/shared-memory demand, occupancy, and independent tile count set crossovers; limits NVIDIA CUDA results to their named hardware and timing boundaries.
depth_and_applicability.limits: The report does not explicitly label the AN5D depth sweep as float/radius-one or itemize the boundary policy reported by each paper. EBISU's double-precision discussion is part of its design model; the report does not establish that as the data type of the quoted 151/197 GCells/s measurement. These source details should be stated or left explicitly unspecified before using the numbers in a precision- or boundary-sensitive comparison.
depth_and_applicability.provenance_and_adoption: No code, helper, test, local product source, or measurement is proposed or adopted. The report gives no SYCL/Intel/Arc crossover or performance prediction.

source_accuracy.status: Both exact arXiv versions and titles were checked; the material numerical claims reviewed against the primary paper PDFs are accurate with one missing precision/boundary context note.
verified: AN5D v4 uses 16,384^2 2D and 512^3 3D domains for 1,000 iterations, five post-warm-up repetitions, and reports averages excluding PCIe time. Its V100 radius-one float depth sweep scales to 10 for 2D, 5 for 3D star, and 3 for 3D box; the paper separately gives first-order tuned-depth ranges of 8–15 in 2D and 3–5 in 3D.

AN5D reports less than half the measured shared-memory bandwidth on P100 versus V100 for identical kernels despite less than 10% difference in measured shared-memory bandwidth; its P100 model can overestimate useful depth. The report preserves this as a target-device-specific result.

EBISU v1 describes A100-PCIe timing as warm-up followed by ten GPU-event measurements of one kernel, reporting the peak. Its analysis says the 2D device-tiling synchronization example yields about 63% useful time versus about 95% valid work for the depth-seven overlap case; the 3D measured comparison is 151 GCells/s without and 197 GCells/s with device tiling.

EBISU's printed 3D shared-memory tile fraction (34 - 2*r*t)^2 / 34^2 evaluates to about 68% for r=1,t=3, not the stated 77%; R876 correctly identifies this inconsistency and does not use 77% as exact arithmetic.
source_accuracy.limits: These are source-paper results on NVIDIA Tesla P100/V100 and A100-PCIe. The two papers do not prove behavior, support, or performance for SYCL or Intel Arc. The scope review did not inspect local product source or run experiments.
